title: Link refusal
description: The body of a coded refusal on a gateway's link, application/json, unsigned: the link's transport authenticates it. The code, the names it concerns, who refused, and the text the session gives the user as the run's error. Every 410 on the link has this body, with the code and the from of the run's end at the gateway, and the state and the reason of that end when it ended the run. A member Forager does not recognise is ignored.

error.description: The refusal code: the gateway's own, or the server's, passed on with its status.

names.description: The names the refusal concerns, as dev.qory.run.refused contains them. A name never carries a value, except the run credential's own value in target_differs_from_credential and differs_from_credential, <member>=<the run credential's value>. Absent when the refusal concerns none.

message.description: The text the session gives the user as the run's error, today's text word for word, on every refusal of the link: the 403, 409, 400 and 410, the server's passed on, and the 500 internal of a run that fails to open for a reason without a code. For a refusal of the server's it names Qory Apiary's URL as today. A session that reads none uses the code. It may span lines: tab and newline are its only control characters, and every other C0 control character, DEL and every C1 control character, U+0080 to U+009F, is refused. It holds no secret, no run credential and no image reference.

from.description: Who refused: gateway, the gateway itself, or apiary, the server, whose refusal the gateway passes on with its code and status.

state.description: On a 410 that ends a run, how the run ended at the gateway: the state of the gateway's own dev.qory.run.exited of it, which the session records in its own dev.qory.run.exited. Absent on every other refusal, and on a 410 of a run that ended otherwise, run_closed.

reason.description: On a 410 that ends a run, the reason of the gateway's own dev.qory.run.exited of it: Forager's code, or the code the run's starter gave. The session records it in its own dev.qory.run.exited, but for a batch the gateway refused, where it records the error, batch_refused. Absent when the run ended with no reason, as when its starter gave an outcome and none, and on every other refusal.
